decisions.evidence: Read the definition and contract. Verified the O/o quantifiers, the zero-of-g convention, O_M uniformity (constants may depend on the fixed machine but not on the input word, its length, or an external clock), transition-count time, visited-cell space as a per-tape initial segment with the explicit n+1 guard, the finite worst-case maximum with the no-words convention, and the separate labelling of read-only input space. No hidden division by g(n), no selection principle, no AC.

Read the definition. Verified canonical binary numerals and unary input including 1^0, the time-constructor requirement to read the whole input and emit bin(t(n)) within Ct(n), the space-constructor visited-cell count, exact-clock constructibility as a separate stronger interface with nonhalting start and a final transition into halt, the external-clock charging rule, and the n+1 guard. Consistent with the cited Arora-Barak Remark 1.5 (T(n)>=n plus a constructor) with an explicit n+1 guard; no equivalence between the flavours is asserted. No AC.

Read the theorem, all sixteen steps and the full contract; re-read Arora-Barak Appendix 1.A printed pp.35-38 (downloaded from the cited URL: 4,572,986 bytes, SHA-256 prefix da0881782a35bde6). Verified the zone capacities and complementary occupancy 0/h_i/2h_i, the ordered redistribution, the reset invariant q_i=H_i=2^i-1 after every event of level at least i (including resets strictly above i), the resulting 2^i separation and at most floor(b/2^i) level-i events, the total O_M(b log(b+2)) time, b=0 and b=1 handling, the origin-bit clamp, lazy archive allocation, the saturated malformed-header check, the left/right-only two-step compilation, and the separate current-configuration space bound O_M(n+S+log(b+2)). Malformed inputs halt rejecting; no AC. Residual sketch-level implementation risk recorded in the contract risk_review.

Read the definition and both verification steps. Verified the standard initial functions, composition with r=0, primitive recursion with k=0 and empty parameter tuples, totality by induction on finite derivation trees, and uniqueness of the recursion solution by applying thm-recursion to the total state map (y,z)->(y+1,h(a,y,z)). No choice; nullary constants included.

Read all six steps. Verified each arithmetic operation is a scheme instance; recomputed the bounded least-witness formula and its B+1 failure value; verified that the cons code is a bijection onto the positive integers with total inverse head/tail, tail(z)<z, the decreasing-iteration length identity, coordinate/append/concatenation folds, and the empty/singleton cases. No appeal from computability to PR; no AC.

Read the definition. Verified length-lex index decoding, the prefix-free tuple encoding E, letters 1/2 for bits with s>=2, the canonical configuration list [q,h,v] and its trim condition against the published configuration and one-step items, the maximal-bit-prefix output convention (empty output invalid; the single bit 0 is numeric zero), and the malformed-program convention matching the published partial-function interface. PR-ness is explicitly deferred to the following lemma, not assumed. No AC.

Read all six steps. Verified each required test is primitive recursive (index decoding, bounded parser, table-shape and range checks, configuration validity, the exact adjacent-step check with clamping, the bounded history conjunction and the total output map with fallback zero) and that the step test is exactly the published one-step relation (untrimmed trailing blanks and spurious nonblank cells are excluded). Determinism gives output uniqueness on all witnesses; genuine finite runs are encoded by finite cons recursion; empty and length-one histories are rejected. No AC.

Read all five steps. Verified the normal form as a consequence of the total PR predicate and witness uniqueness, and the converse compilation of initial functions, strict composition, strict primitive recursion (exactly y h-calls, divergence propagation, y=0 base) and strict minimization (no dovetailing past an undefined value), with explicit finite tape routines and the published one-step interpreter. Domains, including the empty domain, agree; no compiler time bound is asserted. No AC.

Read the definition and both verifications. Verified the direction convention and totality, reflexivity and transitivity for the numeric, oracle and string versions, the one-transition query convention with zero for malformed queries, and the restricted canonical-input/canonical-output numeric-string bridge with its explicit non-claim for unrestricted numeral-image languages. No AC.

Read the definition and both verifications. Verified the query instruction model, the X-computability and X-c.e. definitions, that A<=_T B requires a total decider, that many-one reducibility implies Turing reducibility, and transitivity by simulating the outer decider with total subcalls (a recognizer is explicitly refused at a negative query). Empty oracle, empty query and zero as a valid queried number checked. No AC.

Read the definition and all three verifications. Verified the composition formulation of acceptability, the universal evaluator built from the finite compiler and the published step interpreter, the total code generation with renamed state intervals, delimited zones, canonical table emission and the 2^{|w|}-1+val(w) index, and exact domain/value agreement with divergence propagation. The arity convention and malformed-index divergence are explicit. No AC.

Read all three steps. Verified the generated program parses exactly an n-entry canonical tuple, prepends the m stored parameter blocks under the arity header 1^{m+n}0 and hands the combined tuple to the raw evaluator on e; code generation halts for every input without executing e; the equality of domains and values holds including zero parameters, zero-valued inputs and malformed e; the m=n=1 case reduces to prepending one numeral. No AC.

Read both steps. Verified the binary program q computing H(z,y)=phi_{F(s(z,z))}(y) with f inserted literally, e=s(q,q), the specialization chain giving phi_e=phi_{F(e)} with equality of domains and simultaneous divergence, and the effective index transformation under the totality promise. No AC.

Read the definition and both verifications. Verified the all-input polynomial-time convention, the guarded verifier language with explicit witness polynomial, the 1^{|x|}0xw pair encoding, polynomial many-one reductions with output-length bounds, the output-extent bound from visited cells, the composed polynomial for reduction composition, and the optional fixed-length certificate encoding of 2P+1 bits with P=0 giving the single-letter certificate. Empty inputs and witnesses and the retained guard checked. No AC.

Read the definition and both verifications. Verified the two-table fresh-fair-bit model, the all-branch polynomial bound, the finite space {0,1}^{p(n)} with mass 2^{-p(n)} and prefix mass 2^{-j}, simulator/branch agreement by induction including input-dependent stopping and ignored suffix bits, and the p(n)=0 boundary. Consistent with the cited Arora-Barak Definition 7.1 convention. No AC.

Read the definition and all four verifications. Verified the RP/coRP/BPP thresholds and PP's strict majority, the survival-sum expected time and finite-cutoff min(T,K) identity, q_K<=E T/K by Markov, the 2p(n) truncation bound of 1/2, the fresh-block restart with failure 2^{-(r-1)} and expected cost at most 2P(n), and both directions of ZPP=RP intersect coRP. Empty/full languages and empty input checked; no PP-to-BPP inference. No AC.

Read the definition and both verifications. Verified the count form of pairwise independence, uniform marginals (|F| of |F|^2 seeds per value), the unique seed a=(u-v)(x-y)^{-1} and b=u-ax for distinct inputs with inverse uniqueness, and the explicit inclusion of zero slopes. Singleton D keeps the marginal requirement; collision bounds alone are explicitly not the definition. No AC.

Read all seven steps and recomputed the estimates: 1+u<=exp(u) by the mean value theorem; independence of transforms by finite preimage sums; E exp(lambda S)<=exp(mu(e^lambda-1)); both multiplicative tails by Markov with the prescribed lambda and the explicit rate inequalities delta^2/3 and delta^2/2 verified by their derivatives; delta=1 via P(S=0)=prod(1-p_i)<=e^{-mu}; mu=0, N=0 and delta=0 handled; additive Hoeffding bound via g''=q(1-q)<=1/4, two integrations, Markov at lambda=4t/N and the union bound. Mutual independence is required and stated; all analytic suppliers are declared published items. No AC.

Read all four steps. Verified the integral-domain base case, the decomposition f=sum_j g_j x_m^j with deg g_r<=d-r, the bad-base count, the root bound on each good specialization, the total count dq^{m-1}, the d>=q endpoint, d=0, r=0 and |A|=1. Compared with Arora-Barak Appendix A Lemma A.25 (whole-field case); the nonempty-subset extension is supplied by the same local counting proof. No AC.

Read the example. Verified e=2^{|w|}-1+val(w) as the length-lex index, the compiled addition loop invariant (accumulator a+j, counter y-j), both exact tuple encodings 110 11011 100 and 110 11011 1110100, and the output numerals 11 and 111 with the displayed accumulator trace. The index is the finite compiler output, not an invented decimal. No AC.

Read the example. Verified primality of 5 and F_5=Z/5 by the published prime-field theorem, the inverse table, the unique seed (1,1) for (1,3)->(2,4), the general seed formula a=3(v-u), b=u-a, the 25-seed count including zero slope, and the three-wise failure via h(2)=2h(1)-h(0) with the impossible (h(0),h(1),h(2))=(0,0,1). No AC.

Read the example. Verified the declared field, that X=0 gives no root, the four inverse pairs (1,1),(2,3),(3,2),(4,4), the zero probability 4/25 against the total-degree bound 2/5, and that the comparison is an upper bound rather than an equality. No AC.

Read the page prose against all nineteen authored A items and the manifest. It correctly describes the resource interfaces, the buffered time interpreter and the separate configuration-storing space interpreter, the primitive-recursive coding/history/normal-form/reduction/specialization/fixed-point chain, the finite-bit-string probability development with survival-sum expected time, affine hashing on this page, and formal-polynomial Schwartz-Zippel. The frontmatter item list matches the manifest order exactly, and no page claim exceeds the listed items.

Read the page prose against the three authored examples and the manifest. Each calculation exists and matches the prose (compiled specialization with stored numeral 3, the 25-seed affine family including zero slopes with the three-wise failure, and the four roots of XY-1 against 4/25<2/5). Both field computations declare the prime-field construction. The item list matches the manifest order; placing the three examples under `items:` is legal per SCHEMA.md section 4 ('lists control display placement, not item kind').
